BEFORE THE PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                               OF THE STATE OF MISSOURI

 In the Matter of Evergy Metro, Inc. d/b/a      )
 Evergy Missouri Metro’s Request for            )
 Authority to Implement a General Rate          )            Case No. ER-2026-01431
 Increase for Electric Service                  )


               PUBLIC COUNSEL’S RESPONSE IN OPPOSITION
       TO EVERGY MISSOURI METRO’S MOTION TO STRIKE TESTIMONY

       COMES NOW the Office of Public Counsel (“Public Counsel”) and for its response in

opposition to Evergy Missouri Metro’s motions titled, Evergy Missouri Metro’s Motion to Strike

Portions of the Surrebuttal Testimony of Public Counsel Witnesses David C. Shapley and Paul J.

Alvarez and Motion for Expedited Treatment, states:

       1.      In his direct testimony Mr. Alvarez’s clearly states that “[t]he purpose of my direct

testimony is to present the results of my examination of the reasonableness of EMM’s transmission

and distribution infrastructure spending since the Company’s last rate case, and to provide

recommendations to the Commission regarding EMM capital spending governance.”

       2.      He also clearly states his recommendation that “[t]he Commission should require

discretionary investments that EMM makes or proposes to pass a risk-informed benefit-cost

analysis test of customer cost-effectiveness,” for those investments to qualify for recovery through

retail customer rates.

       3.      Similarly, in his direct testimony Mr. Shapley also clearly states why he is

testifying, “The purpose of my direct testimony is to examine the spending of Evergy Missouri

Metro (EMM) for prudence on behalf of Public Counsel and to provide recommendations to the

Commission regarding EMM’s discretionary spending.

       4.       In paragraph 4 of its motion EMM acknowledges Mr. Alvarez’s purpose is stated

in his direct testimony which Public Counsel prefiled on June 30, 2026.
        5.      EMM has known that Public Counsel witnesses Mr. Alvarez and Mr. Shapley were

evaluating EMM’s discretionary spending on its transmission and distribution system and that they

were recommending EMM be required to conduct a risk-informed benefit-cost analysis test of

customer cost-effectiveness since at least June 30, 2026; it is in no position to claim it was

blindsided with they testified to that same recommendation in their surrebuttal testimony.

       6.      EMM complains in its motion about the magnitude of Public Counsel witnesses

Mr. Alvarez’s and Mr. Shapley’s proposals for the dollar amounts of EMM’s transmission and

distribution spending since its last rate case for which EMM should not recover in retail rates

because EMM is prioritizing distribution and transmission system plant replacement regardless of

the results of objective tests and formal inspections to evaluate the likelihood of service failures.

That is no basis for not allowing their surrebuttal testimony as to those amounts into evidence any

more than not allowing true-up testimony. The real issue is EMM’s criteria for transmission and

distribution spending, not the magnitude of that spending for which EMM should recover from its

retail customers, i.e., the magnitude of EMM’s spending that the Commission should allow EMM

to recover through its retail customers’ rates is a consequence of how EMM decides what and

where to spend on its transmission and distribution system.

       7.      What EMM also omits from its motion is how unreasonably it delayed giving

Public Counsel information wholly within EMM’s control until pressed to do so. That information

includes accounting information about EMM’s transmission and distribution infrastructure

spending which Mr. Alvarez and Mr. Shapley required to be able to quantify the extent to which

that spending is unreasonable.

       8.      Public Counsel reasonably requested information to identify projects to review in

more detail.
        9.      As EMM states, Public Counsel issued its data request 5000 to EMM on April 21,

2026, but EMM did not answer subpart (h) of that request on May 11, 2026. With that subpart

Public Counsel requested “[t]he approved capital spending authorization for the [transmission]

project or program [$250,000 annual aggregate or $250,000 each, respectively], including all

materials Company personnel presented in support of the request.”

       10.     Still not having received the requested information and recognizing that a complete

response to subpart (h) might be overly burdensome, on June 22, 2026, Public Counsel offered to

limit its request in subpart (h) to transmission projects over $3 million rather than over $250,000,

if EMM would provide the requested information promptly.

       11.     On June 29, 2026, EMM responded, “I am told that a supplemental DR response to

5000 will be completed 7/7 for projects over $3M.”

       12.     Public Counsel received EMM’s supplemental response to Public Counsel data

request 5000 on July 9, 2026, which included the following statement, “The attached file provides

the justification for the original project file provided over three million.”

       13.     After finally receiving EMM’s response to Public Counsel data request 5000 (h)

and reviewing it, Public Counsel issued to EMM data requests nos. 5031-5054 on July 27, 2026,

requesting project specific information for projects identified in EMM’s supplemental response to

Public Counsel data request 5000.

       14.     As EMM states in its motion it responded on July 29, 2026, that it would not

respond fully until August 20, 2026. The content of EMM’s email response follows:

       This set of requests is a big lift for us. We will not be able to achieve the deadline.
       We will be able to complete 5031, 5032, and 5049 on time.
       The rest we are requesting an extension to 8/20.

       15.     Pertinent to extensions, Commission rule 20 CSR 4240-2.090(2)(E) states:
        (E) If the recipient asserts an inability to answer the data requests within the twenty
       (20)-day time limit, the recipient shall include the date it will be able to answer the
       data requests simultaneously with its reasons for its inability to answer.

       16.      As EMM represents in its motion, it provided its responses Public Counsel data

requests 5031 and 5032 on August 6, 2026, but despite its July 29, 2026, representation, as EMM

subtlety acknowledges, EMM did not provide its response to Public Counsel data request 5049

until August 20, 2026, when it provided its responses to Public Counsel data requests 5033-5048

and 5050-5054.

       17.      Public Counsel also had difficulty getting timely complete responses to other data

requests it issued to EMM. For example, on August 21, 2026, Public Counsel emailed EMM as

follows:

       It has come to the attention of our experts that Evergy did not provide complete
       responses to some of our requests, specifically to subparts (g) and (h)(vii) & (viii)
       of data request no. 2024. Those requests are:

             2024. Refer to Ryan Mulvaney Direct Testimony, and to the Lateral
             Improvement Program described on page 14. Please provide:
             ****
             g. Any analyses, such as benefit-cost analyses, indicating that the value of
             reliability improvements to customers delivered from this program exceeds
             the incremental costs of the program to customers. If no such analyses have
             been completed, please explain why not.
             h. Provide a list of laterals improved under this program in 2022. For each
             lateral listed, please provide:
             ****

             vii. The counts of customers interrupted and customer minutes of interruption
             on the lateral by year 2019-2021

             viii. The counts of customers interrupted and customer minutes of interruption
             on the lateral by year 2023-2025.

       Evergy’s response to DR 2024 (g) is: “g. The AssetLens tool calculates a benefit-
       to-cost ratio (BCR) based on outage information and age of assets to calculate a
       projected benefit based on reduced outages and outage minutes, utilizing data
       from the ICE calculator, as well as a projected cost to complete the project. A
        BCR greater than 1 suggests that the overall benefits of the project are greater
       than the upfront costs.”

       Evergy’s response to DR 2024 (g) does not show the analyses, at best it identifies
       the methodology.

       Please provide the requested analyses, i.e., the analysis for each lateral
       improvement project. The response should include, for each lateral improvement
       project, at a minimum, the costs per project and benefits estimated by type per
       project (with benefit types per Alexander Rebuttal at 15); customer outage
       benefit; critical outage benefit; restoration benefit; safety benefit; environmental
       benefit; and collateral benefit), but Public Counsel will accept whatever analyses
       Evergy performed.

       Evergy’s responses to DR 2024 (h)(vii) and (h)(viii) include customer minutes of
       interruption by year for each identified period (2019-2021 and 2023-2025),
       neither include the requested counts of customers interrupted.

       Please provide the requested counts of customers interrupted by year for the
       identified periods of 2019-2021 and 2023-2025.

       If you have questions let me know. If Evergy believes a discussion among
       experts would be helpful to getting the information to Public Counsel, let me
       know the availabilities of your experts and I will try to set up a time for a
       conversation to expedite getting responses.

       18.    EMM promptly responded clarifying some of EMM’s responses on that same day

of August 21, 2026, and the parties held the suggested discussion late morning on September 2,

2026, clarifying other of EMM’s responses.

       19.    On August 27, 2026, Public Counsel also issued to EMM another set of data

requests, nos. 5055-5068. EMM objected to Data Request Nos. 5056(c) and (d) as follows:

       The Company objects to these requests to the extent they seek information back to
       2016. The Company has not yet been able to verify whether complete and reliable
       data exist for the full requested period. Given that Evergy Missouri Metro's last
       Missouri rate case was filed in January 2022, the Company submits that 2022
       forward is a more reasonable and proportional time period for these requests.
       Subject to and without waiving these objections, the Company will respond to the
       extent responsive information is available for the period beginning January 1, 2022.
        Notwithstanding and without waiving the foregoing objections, the Company will
       provide answers to the Data Requests.

       20.     By data request 5056 Public Counsel requested the following information:

       Refer to Q2029_Worst Performing Circuit Guidance, which appears to indicate that
       EMM operates a Worst-Performing Lateral (“WPL”) program in addition to its
       worst-performing circuit program. Refer also to Mr. Alexander’s Rebuttal
       Testimony, page 6, which describes the Lateral Improvement program. Please:
        a. Explain the difference between the WPL program and the Lateral Improvement
          Program.
        b. OPC believes to be the Lateral Improvement Program and the program that
          rebuilds laterals to be one and the same. Please confirm or otherwise explain.
        c. Provide i) O&M spending and ii) capital spending on the WPL program by
          year from 2016-2025.
        d. Provide i) O&M spending and ii) capital spending on the Lateral Improvement
          Program by year from 2016-2025.
        e. Provide the threshold used to qualify a lateral worst-performing lateral for
          attention under the worst-performing lateral program.
        f. Provide the threshold used to qualify a lateral for rebuild under the Lateral
          Improvement Program, and explain any relationship to the worst-performing
          lateral program.

       21.     With the ordered surrebuttal filing date of September 10, 2026, impending, Public

Counsel brought EMM’s objection before RLJ Clark at the scheduled September 1, 2026,

discovery conference. Only after that conference did EMM agree to provide the information

requested by subparts c and d back to 2020.

       22.     Despite being the sole source of the information Public Counsel was seeking, EMM

is seeking to have the Commission shift the burden from EMM complying with reasonable

discovery requests to requiring Public Counsel to have the Commission force it to do so.

      Wherefore, the Office of Public Counsel requests the Commission to overrule Evergy

Missouri Metro’s Motion to Strike Portions of the Surrebuttal Testimony of Public Counsel

Witnesses David C. Shapley and Paul J. Alvarez both for its failure to show harm and because

Evergy Missouri Metro unreasonably delayed providing to Public Counsel its cost and other

information regarding its transmission and distribution investments since its last rate case that are
 wholly within the control of Evergy Missouri Metro when responding to Public Counsel’s

discovery requests.

                                                    Respectfully,
